exercise.name: Landmine Squat
library_steps: Hold the free end of a landmine bar at your chest with both hands.
Stand facing the bar, feet shoulder-width apart, leaning slightly into it.
Lower until your thighs are level with the floor.
Stand back up by pressing through your heels.
exercise.one_line_summary: Holding the free end of a landmine bar at the chest with both hands, feet shoulder-width; squat until the thighs are about level, then stand. Quadriceps does the most, glutes and adductors help.

setup.target: Barbell end in a floor pivot in front; the free end held at the chest, cupped in both hands.
setup.why: Library step 1; PARK used landmine exercises.

setup.target: Feet a little wider than the hips, toes slightly out.
setup.why: Library step 2; CLARK: stance width changes activation little.

muscles.emg: Prime mover of the squat; activation rises with load (CLARK).
Prime mover of the squat with the quadriceps (CLARK).
Library secondary; hip extensor in deep squats.

mistakes.what_it_looks_like: Knees fall inside the feet at the bottom.

sources.citation: Park BJ, Jang MY, Seon SY. 2025. The effects of a 16-week periodized linear strength training program incorporating landmine exercises on physical performance in professional female volleyball players. Phys Act Nutr.
sources.what_it_gave: Landmine exercises (barbell end in a floor pivot) used in a 16-week strength programme alongside squats; improved jump power over weights alone.

sources.citation: Clark DR, Lambert MI, Hunter AM. 2012. Muscle activation in the loaded free barbell squat: a brief review. J Strength Cond Res.
sources.what_it_gave: Review of 18 squat EMG studies: prime-mover activation rises with load; stance width, hip rotation and front loading do not change activation much.

clip_check.check: Bar end inside the pivot tube
